title: The definition of negative translation changes the consequent formula name.
details: Handout3 Ch.4 Definition2.1(i), printed p.2, quantifies over Γ and φ but writes: if Γ proves ψ classically, then Γ* proves φ* intuitionistically. The premise ψ should be φ (or the same ψ should occur on both sides). Taken literally with unrelated formulas, the clause would translate a closed proof of a tautology into the translation of falsum; the classical-equivalence clause and Boolean soundness exclude that. This is a local letter mismatch; using the same formula on both sides repairs the definition. Adjacent planning inspection only: no current entry adopts this malformed clause, and no upstream correction is inferred.
